name: DataBank Dallas Empire Central Data Center

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading:
DataBank DFW4 sits at 1100 Empire Central Place, Dallas, Texas, one of roughly ten DataBank facilities across the Dallas-Fort Worth metro. DataBank's own facility page states 35,900 square feet of IT space and 4 megawatts of critical IT load, built to an N+1 power and N+1 cooling design, with SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI DSS, and ISO 27001 compliance certifications. DataBank does not state a year-opened date or name the power utility on DFW4's page; Oncor is the incumbent transmission and distribution utility across the Dallas-Fort Worth metro as a matter of public record and is explicitly named by DataBank on its Plano and Red Oak campus materials, though not specifically for DFW4. Across its full Dallas-Fort Worth portfolio, DataBank states a combined 866,640 square feet of IT space and 193.8 megawatts of critical IT load across ten facilities, reflecting the metro's status as DataBank's home market since the company's 2005 founding in Dallas. The Empire Central corridor sits in Dallas's Stemmons Freeway-adjacent industrial and office district, near Dallas Love Field, an area with a longstanding concentration of telecommunications and data infrastructure tenants predating the more recently developed suburban campuses in Plano, Richardson, and Red Oak. DataBank has separately announced a new 480 megawatt "Red Oak" campus south of Dallas, a 292-acre site with up to eight buildings on a 400 megawatt Oncor substation targeting initial service in Q2 2026, underscoring continued expansion in the broader DFW metro alongside established smaller facilities like DFW4.

Dallas's Stemmons Freeway-adjacent industrial corridor, home to DFW4 and the nearby historic Infomart carrier hotel, developed as an early telecommunications and data infrastructure hub in the 1990s, well before Plano's Legacy Park and the newer Red Oak campus emerged as DataBank's larger-scale suburban growth markets. DataBank's continued Texas expansion, anchored by its Dallas headquarters, reflects the broader Texas data center boom that has drawn hyperscale and colocation investment statewide, prompting ERCOT to substantially revise its long-term electricity demand forecasts upward to account for data center and other large-load growth across the state.

profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-03, batch 97 (DataBank): operator own dedicated page confirmed the existing address and added IT capacity and sqft, research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to DataBank. DataBank Ltd. was established in 2005 in a historic former Federal Reserve Bank building in downtown Dallas, Texas, that had been converted to a data center in 1999, per DataBank own corporate history page fetched this session. DataBank was acquired in July 2016 by a group of investors led by DigitalBridge, per that same page. DataBank own history page also lists a series of acquisitions expanding its footprint, three Salt Lake City area data centers from C7 Data Centers plus facilities in Cleveland and Pittsburgh from 365 Data Centers in January 2017, Lightbound, an Indianapolis based provider, in December 2018, United States and United Kingdom data center assets from zColo in December 2020, and four Houston area data centers from CyrusOne for 670 million dollars in January 2022. A trade press article fetched this session, from pe-insights.com, reports that DigitalBridge agreed to sell a 27 percent fully diluted equity stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management and EDF Invest for about 1.2 billion dollars, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, reducing DigitalBridge own stake to about 15.5 percent and yielding DigitalBridge about 230 million dollars in cash proceeds. DataBank own history page states the company now operates more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets. The operator own dedicated page for this facility, Dallas Empire Central, designated DFW4, fetched this session, confirms the address already on file, 1100 Empire Central Place, Dallas, TX 75247, and states 4 MW of critical IT load and 35,900 IT square feet.

reading.body:
DataBank Dallas Empire Central publishes 4 MW of IT capacity across 35,900 square feet at 1100 Empire Central Place in Dallas, making it the smallest facility by capacity among Texas data centers tracked here for which a megawatt figure is public.

At 40 kW per rack, a density used for AI training clusters, 4 MW supports roughly 100 racks. At 10 kW per rack, typical for colocation, the same power supports roughly 400 racks. This gap is material: the facility's actual compute density is not published. By current standards for large-scale AI infrastructure, where single training clusters consume multiples of 4 MW, this campus represents a modest footprint.

The facility holds a FedRAMP certification, qualifying it for U.S. federal cloud workloads under the government's security authorization framework. No other certifications are published. This positions the facility for regulated government work rather than as a site for large-scale AI training or inference deployment.

Across 13 Texas facilities in this dataset that publish capacity figures, totaling 389 MW, Empire Central ranks last at 4 MW, representing roughly one percent of the state's published total. For readers assessing where significant AI compute concentration exists, this location is not a material driver of capacity growth or clustering.
